map.估算低钠血症治疗中血钠上升速度。: Work out the safe sodium correction rate and the infusion rate needed to raise serum sodium without exceeding the daily limit that risks osmotic demyelination.
map.📖 查看「低钠血症纠正速度 使用指南」: 📖 View the "Hyponatraemia Correction Rate User Guide"
map.血钠变化 ≈ (输注液钠 − 当前血钠) / (总体水 + 1): Change in serum sodium ≈ (infusate sodium − current serum sodium) / (total body water + 1)
map.仅为教学估算，临床必须个体化治疗。: A teaching estimate only; clinical treatment must be individualised.
map.📚 深度解析：低钠血症纠正速度估算: 📚 Deep Dive: Hyponatraemia Correction Rate Estimation
map.教学演示：估算补钠后血钠预期升幅: Teaching demo: estimate the expected rise in serum sodium after sodium replacement
map.安全边界：提示 24h 血钠上升不超 8–10 mmol/L: Safety boundary: a reminder that the 24h rise in serum sodium should not exceed 8-10 mmol/L
map.风险意识：过快纠正可致渗透性脱髓鞘: Risk awareness: correcting too fast can cause osmotic demyelination
map.算法（简化教学）：预期升幅 = (输注液钠浓度 − 当前血钠) ÷ (总体水+1: Algorithm (simplified teaching): expected rise = (infusate sodium − current serum sodium) ÷ (total body water + 1); target gap = target serum sodium − current serum sodium; with a 24h cap reminder (8-10 mmol/L). Teaching only; clinical use must be individualised.
map.例1（输注液钠 154、总体水 42L、目标 130、当前 118）：预期升幅: Example 1 (infusate sodium 154, total body water 42 L, target 130, current 118): expected rise (154−118)/(42+1) = 0.84 mmol/L, target gap 12.0 mmol/L. Example 2 (total body water 35 L, target 135, current 120): rise (154−120)/36 = 0.94 mmol/L, gap 15.0 mmol/L (a large gap calls for even slower correction).
map.为什么不能补太快？: Why can't sodium be replaced too fast?
map.血钠纠正过快（>8–10 mmol/L/24h）可诱发渗透性脱髓鞘综合征，严重致: Correcting serum sodium too fast (>8-10 mmol/L/24h) can trigger osmotic demyelination syndrome with severe disability; chronic hyponatraemia especially requires slow correction, often limited to 4-6 mmol/L/24h.
map.这能当医嘱吗？: Can this be used as a medical order?
map.不能，属教学估算；真实补钠需结合容量状态（低容/等容/高容）、尿电解质与内分泌评: No, it is a teaching estimate; real sodium replacement must consider volume status (hypovolaemic/euvolemic/hypervolaemic), urine electrolytes and endocrine assessment, and be set by a doctor.
